headline: TrailWing: An Offline Bird Call Identifier Works Where Your Signal Doesn't
summary: TrailWing is an open-source, offline-first birding companion that identifies bird calls locally. It uses open-weight models and local 'trail packs' to work without cell service, ensuring privacy and community customization.
details: TrailWing is an open-source, offline-first birding companion designed for use in areas without cell service. Before heading out, users download small "trail packs" containing expected bird species and local weather forecasts for their chosen location.

When a bird call is heard, users press a button to record a 10-second audio clip. A local open-weight model then processes the clip against the downloaded trail pack, providing a likely identification with a confidence score and a tip for visual confirmation.

The app encourages outdoor engagement through light "field quests," such as finding different songs or spotting feeding birds. These quests are designed to promote active observation rather than screen scrolling.
TrailWing is aimed at beginner and intermediate birders, hikers, and families who want to learn about local birds without relying on cell service or sharing their location data with external servers.
The project's reliance on open-weight models allows all inference to run locally on the device, ensuring full functionality even in remote areas with zero signal, which is critical for birding.
Privacy is a core feature: audio recordings and location data never leave the device. Only the trail chosen by the user is communicated to the server, protecting personal information.

The open-source nature of TrailWing also enables community improvements. Regional birding clubs can fine-tune or swap models for local species, adjust prompts for specific call dialects, or even host their own trail-pack servers, all without vendor dependency or per-request costs.
